mainTopic: An idol that broke by itself and the nest in an אשירה tree; then wood bought by the גזברים and שמואל's rule that the בית המקדש is built with חולין.
overview: The גמרא opens with a מחלוקת about an idol that broke by itself. רבי יוחנן says it is still forbidden because no non-Jew cancelled it. ריש לקיש says it is permitted because the owner gives up on an idol that could not even save itself. ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from our משנה, which lets a person knock down a nest in an אשירה tree with a pole, as if branches that broke off the idol are permitted. The first answer, that the bird brought wood from elsewhere, is attacked from the הקדש half of the משנה. So the גמרא reads the case as branches that grew after the tree was consecrated, and it backs this up from the pole. רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, keeps the outside-wood reading and says the pole is for knocking down the chicks. The גמרא then rules that chicks are permitted and eggs are forbidden, and רב אשי adds that chicks still needing their mother count like eggs. A new משנה teaches that there is מעילה on wood the גזברים bought, but not on its sawdust or leaves. שמואל explains that building is done with חולין: the donated money's holiness is moved onto the finished building, and then the money is paid to the workers.

steps.title: Dispute: an idol that broke by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether an idol that broke on its own is still forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: It was stated: An idol that broke by itself — רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden, and ריש לקיש says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument (an איתמר). Two great אמוראים disagree about an idol that broke all by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an idol stays forbidden for benefit until it is cancelled (בטול). The question is whether breaking by itself, with nobody cancelling it, is enough to make it permitted. רבי יוחנן says no and ריש לקיש says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol or object of idol worship, which is forbidden for any benefit
That broke by itself, with nobody breaking it
Forbidden (here, forbidden for benefit)
Permitted

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
An idol that broke by itself:
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: It is forbidden.
And Reish Lakish says: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a related מחלוקת about עבודה זרה, which comes up in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an idol that broke by itself stays forbidden. ריש לקיש: it becomes permitted.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why each side holds the way he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden, because no non-Jew cancelled it. ריש לקיש says it is permitted, because the owner says to himself: 'It could not even save itself, so will it save me?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for each opinion from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, an idol only loses its status when a non-Jew actively cancels it, and here no one did. For ריש לקיש, we assume the owner gives up on a broken idol by himself, because it obviously has no power. That giving up counts as cancelling it.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelled it (removed its idol status)
A non-Jew; only he can cancel an idol
It itself
Saves or protects

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying a broken idol stops being an idol automatically. He is saying we assume the owner gives up on it, and that counts as cancelling it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says it is forbidden
because a non-Jew did not cancel it.
And Reish Lakish says it is permitted
because he will say:
phrases.notes: "He" is the non-Jew who owns the idol.

phrases.english: It could not even save itself,
will it save me?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אֲסוּרָה דְּלָא בַּטְּלַהּ גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two rulings in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן requires active בטול by a non-Jew. ריש לקיש assumes the owner gives up on a broken idol, and that counts as בטול.

steps.title: ריש לקיש quotes the משנה about a nest
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן by quoting the משנה about a nest in a הקדש tree and a nest in an אשירה tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: A nest at the top of a הקדש tree — one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. A nest in an אשירה — one may knock it down with a pole.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a source from the משנה to argue against רבי יוחנן. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains how it is a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is about the אשירה, a tree that is worshipped. The משנה lets a person knock the nest down with a pole and take it. That suggests the nest itself is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's nest
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
Liable for מעילה, the misuse of הקדש property
A tree that is worshipped as an idol
Knock it down with a pole

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
A nest at the top of a tree of הקדש:
One may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misuse.
A nest in an אשירה tree: one knocks it down with a pole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's position from step 2 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that something that came off an idol by itself stays forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits taking the nest from an אשירה. This is explained fully in step 4.

steps.title: The nest is made of branches that broke off the idol
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains: the nest must be from branches that broke off the אשירה by themselves, and yet the משנה permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the משנה talking about branches that broke off the tree itself? And still it teaches that one may knock the nest down with a pole!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש spells out his challenge. He says the nest is made from pieces of the idol that broke off by themselves, and the משנה still permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches that fell off the אשירה are like an idol that broke by itself, since no non-Jew cancelled them. If the משנה permits the nest, broken pieces of an idol must be permitted. That supports ריש לקיש and goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...? (introduces a proposed reading)
That broke off from the tree itself

phrases.english: Is it not talking about branches that broke off from the tree itself,
and yet it teaches: one knocks it down with a pole?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 3 challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that something broken off an idol by itself stays forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nest is made from branches that broke off the idol by themselves, yet the משנה permits it. So self-broken parts of an idol are permitted.

steps.title: No, the bird brought wood from elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The answer for רבי יוחנן: the משנה is talking about a nest built from outside wood, not from the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה is talking about a case where the bird brought wood from somewhere else.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's side pushes back. The nest in the משנה does not have to come from the idol tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bird built the nest from outside sticks, those sticks were never part of the idol. They are permitted no matter what. So the משנה says nothing about an idol that broke by itself, and רבי יוחנן's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Sticks or pieces of wood
From elsewhere (literally, 'from the world')

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's first defense is to read the משנה as a nest made of outside wood. The next step challenges this answer.

phrases.english: No, it is where it brought wood from elsewhere.
phrases.notes: "It" is the bird that built the nest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by reading the משנה as a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defines the case in the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nest was built from branches that broke off the אשירה itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nest was built from outside wood that was never part of the idol.

steps.title: If the nest is from outside wood, why is the הקדש nest forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges the answer of step 5. If the nest was built from outside wood, the הקדש nest should be fully permitted. So why does the משנה forbid benefiting from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say that with a הקדש tree, one may not benefit from the nest, but one is not liable for מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer given for רבי יוחנן, that the nest was made from outside wood. It points to the first half of the same משנה, about a הקדש tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה says that a nest in a הקדש tree is forbidden for benefit, even though there is no מעילה. If the nest were from ordinary outside wood, it should not be forbidden at all. So the 'outside wood' explanation does not fit the הקדש half of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if we accept what you just said
One may not benefit from it (forbidden from the start)
One is not liable for מעילה (misusing holy property), even if he did benefit

phrases.english: If so, why is the nest in a consecrated tree
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if the nest was built from outside wood, as step 5 said.

phrases.english: forbidden for benefit, though one is not liable for misuse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 5 by using the הקדש half of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the nest was built from outside wood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outside wood has no holiness, so the הקדש nest should be fully permitted. Yet the משנה forbids benefit from it.

steps.title: The משנה is about branches that grew after the tree was consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'outside wood' idea. The nest is made from the tree's own branches that grew after it was consecrated. The תנא holds that there is no מעילה on such later growths, but benefiting from them is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about growths that came later, and the תנא holds there is no מעילה on growths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the משנה that fits the הקדש case. The nest's branches grew on the tree after it became הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later growths of a הקדש tree are a middle level: forbidden to use, but with no מעילה. That explains exactly why the משנה says 'no benefit, but no מעילה.' The 'אלא' drops the outside-wood answer of step 5, so the nest is again made from the tree's own branches, and ריש לקיש's challenge against רבי יוחנן from the אשירה case is back.

keyTerms.meaning: Growths: new parts that grew on something after a certain point
Afterward: here, after the tree was consecrated
He holds: introduces the opinion this תנא follows

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the growths are not הקדש at all. They are still forbidden to use. The only difference is that there is no מעילה penalty for using them.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about growths
that came afterward,
and he holds one is not liable for misusing growths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by replacing the outside-wood reading with a reading about later growths.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nest was built from outside wood, so it has no connection to the tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nest is built from the tree's own branches that grew after consecration. These are forbidden for benefit but carry no מעילה.

steps.title: Proof: why else knock the nest down with a pole?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the new reading. For the אשירה tree, the משנה says to knock the nest down with a pole. If the nest were from outside wood, a person could simply take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you think the bird brought the wood from elsewhere, why must he knock it down with a pole? Let him just take it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that the nest is made from the tree's own wood, not outside wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that in the אשירה case one must knock the nest down with a pole. That makes sense only if the nest itself is connected to the forbidden tree. If the nest were from outside wood, it would be ordinary and could be taken by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: This also makes sense: the גמרא is bringing support
If it enters your mind: if you were to think
He should knock it down or dislodge it
A pole or reed

phrases.english: This too stands to reason,
for if it enters your mind
that the bird brought the wood from elsewhere,
why should he knock it down with a pole?
Let him just take it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of step 7 that the nest comes from the tree itself.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the nest is made from the tree's own wood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's instruction to knock down the אשירה nest with a pole rather than take it directly.

steps.title: The nest is from outside wood, and "knock down" means the chicks
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, rejects the proof. The nest really is from outside wood. The pole is used to knock down the chicks, not the nest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: really, the bird brought the wood from elsewhere. And what does 'knock down' mean? Knock down the chicks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends רבי יוחנן. He rejects the proof from the pole by explaining that the pole is for the chicks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that 'knock down' was about the nest itself. רבי אבהו says it is about the chicks inside, which cannot simply be picked up without climbing the tree. So the pole does not show that the nest is forbidden wood, and the outside-wood reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really: we go back to the original explanation
Chicks: baby birds

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's side keeps its reading that the nest is from outside wood. The pole in the אשירה case is for getting the chicks down, so the משנה does not prove that a self-broken idol is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Actually, the bird brought the wood from elsewhere,
and what does "knock down" mean?
He knocks down the chicks.
phrases.notes: Chicks move around, so without a pole he might climb the tree to grab them. Using the tree that way is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 and restores the outside-wood reading of step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the pole, not the whole discussion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that 'knock down' referred to the nest. It actually refers to the chicks.

steps.title: Chicks are permitted, eggs are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב tells רבי ירמיה that chicks from either tree are permitted, but eggs from either tree are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה: Chicks, both here and there, are permitted. Eggs, both here and there, are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 9 said the pole knocks down the chicks, so now the גמרא gives the clear ruling about the chicks and the eggs in the nest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule applies to the הקדש tree and the אשירה tree. Chicks are permitted to use, but eggs are forbidden. Eggs still sit in the nest and depend on the forbidden tree, while chicks can fly off and are not tied to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Eggs
Here and there, meaning in both cases
Permitted / forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said to Rabbi Yirmeya:
Chicks, here and there, are permitted.
phrases.notes: "Here and there" means both the הקדש tree and the אשירה tree.

phrases.english: Eggs, here and there, are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 9's point that the pole knocks down the chicks, and gives the final ruling for chicks and eggs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chicks from a הקדש tree or an אשירה tree are permitted. Eggs from either tree are forbidden.

steps.title: Young chicks that need their mother count like eggs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits the permission for chicks: if they still need their mother, they are treated like eggs and are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If the chicks still need their mother, they are like eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to the rule in step 10 about chicks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 permitted chicks in general. רב אשי says that only applies to chicks that can manage on their own. Chicks too young to survive without their mother are still tied to the nest, so they take the forbidden status of eggs.

keyTerms.meaning: Need their mother, too young to live on their own
They are like eggs, they have the same status as eggs

steps.whatToRemember: Chicks are permitted, eggs are forbidden, and chicks still dependent on their mother are forbidden like eggs.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If the chicks need their mother,
they are like eggs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אִם אֶפְרוֹחִים צְרִיכִין לְאִמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to step 10's permission for chicks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chicks that still depend on their mother have the status of eggs and are forbidden.

steps.title: New משנה: wood bought by the treasurers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that when the גזברים buy logs, there is מעילה on the wood itself, but not on the sawdust or the leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When the treasurers bought wood, one is liable for מעילה on the wood, but not on the sawdust and not on the leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about wood that the גזברים bought for the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wood itself became הקדש, so misusing it brings מעילה. The leftover sawdust and leaves are not part of what was bought for building, so there is no מעילה on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Treasurers of the בית המקדש
Sawdust or shavings from cutting wood
Leaves or twigs that fall off the log

phrases.english: MISHNA: The treasurers who bought wood:
one is liable for misusing the wood,
but one is not liable for misusing the sawdust,
nor the leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the nest discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is מעילה on wood bought by the גזברים, but not on its sawdust or leaves.

steps.title: Build first with non-holy materials, then make them holy
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that construction in the בית המקדש is done with חולין materials, and they are made הקדש only afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: We build with non-holy materials, and afterward we make them holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's rule about how building work in the בית המקדש is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The materials are not holy while the building is going up. Only after the work is done does the building become הקדש. The next steps explain the reason for this method.

keyTerms.meaning: We build
Non-holy, ordinary
We make holy, consecrate

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
We build with non-holy materials,
and afterward we make them holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בּוֹנִין בַּחוֹל וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַקְדִּישִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives background to the משנה about the treasurers' wood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building in the בית המקדש is done with חולין, and the building is made הקדש after it is finished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets the pattern for how the בית המקדש handled building materials, and the next steps explain the reason for it.

steps.title: Why build with non-holy materials?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we don't make the materials holy right away. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for the logic behind שמואל's rule, not an attack on it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are the building materials kept חולין until the work is done?

steps.title: Donated money is holy, so its holiness moves onto the building
steps.stepSummary: Whoever donates money makes it holy. The treasurer therefore declares that the money's holiness should rest on the finished building.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever donates money makes it holy, so the treasurer says: 'Let the holiness of the money take effect on the building.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer why we build with חולין. The next step completes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Donated money is הקדש, so paying workers or suppliers with it directly would cause מעילה. To avoid this, the treasurer moves the money's holiness onto the finished building. That is why the materials stay חולין until the building is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Donates, gives as a free-will gift
Money, coins
Let it take effect, let it rest on
Holiness
The building

steps.confusionAlert: The holiness does not go onto the wood or stones while they are being built. It goes onto the finished building, which is why the materials are still חולין during the work.

phrases.english: Whoever donates money
makes it holy,
so he says: "Let the holiness of the money take effect on the building,"

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Donated money is holy, so its holiness is moved onto the finished building. That keeps the materials and the workers' pay from being holy during construction.

steps.title: The now-unholy money is paid to the workers
steps.stepSummary: After the holiness passes from the money to the finished building, the treasurers give the money to the craftsmen as their wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then he gives it to the craftsmen as their pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to why construction is done with חולין materials. Once the building is done and holy, the money is free to be paid to the workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money had stayed הקדש, paying workers with it would be מעילה, using holy property for ordinary purposes. Because the treasurer moved the holiness onto the building, the money becomes חולין. Now it can be handed to the workers with no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Craftsmen or artisans who do the building work
Their wages, their pay
And he gives (the treasurer gives the money)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule works like this: build with חולין materials, then move the money's holiness onto the finished building, and then pay the workers with the now-חולין money.

phrases.english: And he gives it to the craftsmen
phrases.notes: "He" is the treasurer, and "it" is the money, which isn't holy anymore since its holiness moved onto the building.

phrases.english: as their wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 15 by showing the practical result: the money, now חולין, can pay the workers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reason for building with חולין is so that, after the holiness moves to the building, the money is חולין and can be given to the workers as wages without מעילה.
